name: El Taller
description: A year running a small independent car-repair workshop in Leon, Guanajuato, Mexico (fictional): five technicians, four lifts, one delivery fleet and a tight cash position. Decision 1 (January, quoting): the price of the labour hour (the street price, a price costed from the shop costs and the hours it actually bills, or a dealership premium); how jobs are quoted (a verbal estimate, a written quote with the customer authorising any extra, or quoting low and adding extras at delivery); the diagnosis (free, skipped by changing parts until the fault goes, or paid and credited to the repair). Decision 2 (April, bays and technicians): how cars come in (first come first served, every car promised the same day, or appointments built from standard times with cars waiting for parts moved off the lifts); who does what (whoever is free, assignment by skill, or every hard job to the best technician); what happens before delivery (the technician signs off, hand over untested to keep the promise, or a road test and checklist by a second technician). Decision 3 (July, parts and the fleet): the parts shelf (a large promotional pack, no stock with every part ordered per job, or only the fast movers with minimum and maximum levels); which parts are fitted (the cheapest, known-brand new parts with warranty, or used parts billed as new); a delivery fleet asking for a discount and 60 days of credit (accept, refuse, or a written contract with 30 days, a credit limit and booked slots). Decision 4 (October, before the year-end season): season prices (a discount campaign, keep prices, or a fixed-price menu from standard times); capacity (Saturday overtime, a fifth lift, or an apprentice from a dual-training programme); the used oil (drums in the yard, sold to an informal collector, or an authorised collector with manifests). The model is deterministic and monthly: technician hours are the constraint, hours per job come from standard times, comebacks consume unbilled capacity, on-time delivery falls with load, reputation moves demand, and the parts shelf and fleet receivables take cash out of the bank. The score combines the quality of each decision with the year profit, the lowest month-end cash, on-time delivery, comebacks and compliance, and is capped when a decision breaks the rules (unauthorised charges, used parts billed as new, used oil to an informal collector). Spanish (primary, Mexico) and English.
view:
Eureka Express · El Taller

El Taller

Un año al frente de un taller mecánico independiente en León, Guanajuato: cinco técnicos, cuatro elevadores y una caja que no alcanza. En cuatro decisiones usted pone precio a la hora, programa las bahías y a los técnicos, decide qué refacciones tener y cómo crecer en la temporada sin ahogarse.

Situación

Decisión 1 · Cotizar

Lo que decida rige todo el año. Mientras no decida lo demás, el cálculo supone las opciones que vienen marcadas en las decisiones siguientes: primero en llegar, el técnico que esté libre y que él mismo firme; el paquete de la promoción, la refacción más barata y la flota con sus condiciones; el descuento, horas extra los sábados y los tambos.

Decisión 2 · Bahías y técnicos

Lo que decida rige de abril a diciembre. De enero a marzo el taller trabajó como siempre: primero en llegar, el que esté libre y cada técnico firma su trabajo.

Decisión 3 · Refacciones y la flota

Lo que decida rige de julio a diciembre. Hasta junio el taller usó el anaquel viejo y la refacción más barata.

Decisión 4 · Crecer sin ahogarse

Lo que decida rige de octubre a diciembre, en la temporada alta.
